title: In-Process Financial Log Analytics
business: Financial analysts performing ad-hoc risk assessments on high-volume transaction logs.
problem: Traditional client-server databases introduce significant latency due to network overhead and serialization costs when analysts need to query multi-gigabyte transaction logs stored locally.
solution: DuckDB provides an in-process analytical engine that embeds directly into the analyst's Python environment, allowing SQL queries to run against local files without the need for a separate database server or data movement.
steps: Install the DuckDB Python package within the local analysis environment.
Point the engine to the directory containing raw transaction logs in Parquet or CSV format.
Execute SQL queries directly against the files using the vectorized execution engine.
Leverage the in-process architecture to perform joins and aggregations without exporting data to an external server.
outcome: Analysts achieve near-instantaneous query results on local datasets, eliminating the infrastructure maintenance and network bottlenecks associated with traditional database servers.
limitation: Because DuckDB runs embedded within the host process, it shares memory and CPU resources with the host application; heavy analytical queries may impact the performance of other tasks running in the same process, which can be monitored by observing system resource utilization during query execution.

diagram.title: In-Process Data Flow
diagram.description: Shows how DuckDB bypasses external servers to access local data.

code.content:
import duckdb
# Query local files directly without importing data
results = duckdb.query("SELECT category, SUM(amount) FROM 'logs/*.parquet' GROUP BY category").df()
code.explanation: This demonstrates the in-process capability where the engine reads files directly from the local filesystem into the Python environment.
